explanation: Direct semantic match for milk, curd, paneer, butter, cheese, and yogurt.
ambiguities_or_limitations: In Indian retail, eggs are occasionally cataloged under Dairy (e.g. mockData p5 'Farm Fresh Eggs' has category 'Dairy'), whereas Kaggle model has a dedicated 'EGGS' family.

explanation: Direct match for bread, buns, pav, rusks, cakes, and fresh bakery items.
ambiguities_or_limitations: Indian Kirana bakery products have ultra-short shelf life (2-3 days for pav/bread), whereas model includes long-life packaged bakery goods.

explanation: Direct match for packaged soft drinks, sodas, bottled water, and juices.
ambiguities_or_limitations: In Indian retail, packaged tea and coffee (e.g. Assam Tea) are often categorized as Beverages, whereas international grocery taxonomy often places dry tea leaves in GROCERY I.

explanation: Direct match for soaps, shampoos, oral care, hair care, deodorants, and sanitary goods.
ambiguities_or_limitations: Kaggle dataset splits BEAUTY and BABY CARE into separate families. ShopPulse's Personal Care collapses these distinct segments.

explanation: Covers cleaning consumables such as detergents, dishwash bars, floor disinfectants (Lizol), and surface cleaners.
ambiguities_or_limitations: Kaggle has separate families for CLEANING, HOME CARE, and HOME AND KITCHEN. Indian retailers mix cleaning agents with kitchen plastics and pest control under Household.

explanation: Standard dry packaged food goods, packaged condiments, and processed shelf-stable foods.
ambiguities_or_limitations: In Indian retail, 'Groceries' is often an ambiguous catch-all category or default OCR fallback, spanning products that should be in Staples, Snacks, or Spices.

explanation: Instant noodles (Maggi), biscuits, chips, wafers, namkeen, and savory snacks.
ambiguities_or_limitations: Kaggle model has NO dedicated 'SNACKS' family. In Corporación Favorita, all snack foods were rolled into the massive GROCERY I family. Mapping is forced into GROCERY I.

explanation: Atta (wheat flour), rice, pulses (dal), edible cooking oils, salt, and refined sugar.
ambiguities_or_limitations: Staples account for ~50% of Indian Kirana volume, often sold in high-weight packaging (5kg-25kg bags) with bulk purchasing dynamics not reflected in Kaggle GROCERY I.

explanation: Rice, wheat, millets, semolina (sooji), and whole grains (seen in backend tests).
ambiguities_or_limitations: Sub-category of Indian Staples; maps to dry goods in GROCERY I.

explanation: Packaged tea biscuits, cookies, and cream biscuits (seen in backend tests).
ambiguities_or_limitations: Branded packaged biscuits belong to GROCERY I, but could overlap with BREAD/BAKERY if fresh.

explanation: Cooking oils such as mustard, sunflower, groundnut, and edible ghee (seen in backend tests).
ambiguities_or_limitations: Must be mapped to GROCERY I (edible oils) and strictly prevented from mapping to AUTOMOTIVE (motor oils).

explanation: Dry spices, masalas, turmeric, chili powder, coriander (seen in backend tests).
ambiguities_or_limitations: Dry packaged seasoning is part of GROCERY I, but bulk unbranded whole spices behave more like agricultural commodities.
